title: U.S. Senate · Rhode Island

context.text: This is the Class II U.S. Senate seat held by Jack Reed, who first took office in 1997. Reed defeated Connor Burbridge and Luis Daniel Muñoz in the September 9, 2026 Democratic primary, 76.8%-13.5%-9.7%. Raymond McKay ran unopposed for the Republican nomination after Allen Waters withdrew. Michael Bahry is running as an independent; a fourth candidate, Jon Lindley (independent), withdrew or was disqualified before the general election.

positions.summary: Sponsored S. 1903, a bill to prohibit changes to Medicare and Medicaid in reconciliation legislation.

Cosponsored S. 2150, the Women's Health Protection Act of 2025, a bill to protect a person's ability to determine whether to continue or end a pregnancy and a provider's ability to provide abortion services.
Cosponsored S. 3214, the Background Check Expansion Act, a bill to require a background check for every firearm sale.
Cosponsored S. 2845, the Billionaires Income Tax Act, a bill to require billionaires to pay taxes annually by modifying provisions that allow them to defer tax indefinitely.
Cosponsored S. 1332, the Raise the Wage Act of 2025, a bill to provide for increases in the federal minimum wage.
Cosponsored S. 5390, the End Trump's Tariff Tax Act, a bill to terminate and refund certain duties imposed by the President.

record.text: For the 2025-2026 Congress, serves as Ranking Member of the Senate Armed Services Committee, Ranking Member of the Appropriations Subcommittee on Financial Services and General Government, and a member of the Senate Committee on Banking, Housing, and Urban Affairs and the Select Committee on Intelligence.
Chaired the Senate Armed Services Committee and the Appropriations Subcommittee on the Legislative Branch during the 2023-2024 Congress.

candidates.name: Raymond McKay

priorities.text: Curbing federal government spending, which he says drives inflation and economic pressure on Rhode Islanders.
Securing the border and enforcing immigration law.
Strengthening Social Security and Medicare, and supporting veterans and the military.

candidates.researchNotes: Positions and priorities are drawn from McKay's 2024 Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey (for a prior run for this same seat); he has not completed a 2026 survey and no updated policy page was found on his 2026 campaign site. Statements added from the Right Direction page of his 2026 campaign website, which states priorities in general terms without taking sides on specific guide issues.

statements.quote: Ray is committed to addressing responsible immigration and enforcement policies that consider the best interest of Rhode Islanders and Americans First.
statements.context: On the Right Direction page of his campaign website

statements.quote: Ray is committed to American energy independence getting colleagues on both sides of the aisle to work together for long-term strength and stability of our nuclear and fossil fuel industries and efficiently utilizing green energy solutions.
statements.context: On the Right Direction page of his campaign website

candidates.name: Michael Bahry

priorities.text: Ending U.S. participation in what he calls "endless wars," saying it makes the world less safe rather than more.
Running as an independent so he can vote issue-by-issue without party loyalty.
Addressing the national debt, which he says has been driven up by career politicians.

positions.summary: Criticizes spending on mass deportations and says he wants a compassionate solution rather than removal of long-resident workers; also says the border must be secured to stop human and drug trafficking.
positions.quote: We're spending billions on mass deportations while our legal immigration system stays broken.

statements.quote: I am Catholic and I am pro-life.
statements.context: On the platform page of his campaign website

candidates.researchNotes: Immigration and abortion are from the platform page of his campaign website. His Gaza/war views appear there only as video titles (no transcript), so no Israel-aid stance or statement is recorded.
